title: Modus II: from printed letters to German

facsimile.region_note: Printed p. 57 is HAB image 249 and corpus image 251. The detail shows the significant letters and the beginning of the cover text. The full page also shows the alphabet and the German Intentio.

passage.label: German Intentio in the reading edition
passage.note: The structured rendering keeps its published passage ID. The corresponding continuous Latin OCR is in segment 124.

cover.label: Exemplum secundi (complete cover prayer)
cover.method: Count the printed prayer from Creator through Amen. Join line-end divisions and expand the abbreviated words as consequamur and miserosque. The subscription follows the prayer.

cipher_stream.label: Literae significantes
cipher_stream.method: The two lines preserve the photographed letter order and the long s. Spaces separate individual types. For calculation, lowercase G, write ſ as s and omit punctuation. The previous transcription repeated the s between v and k.

extraction.rule: Read the significant-letter line in order. Independently take the initial of each even word in the cover prayer.

decode.rule: The print moves each plaintext letter two places back on its 22-letter circle. Invert the 22 printed pairs and substitute for each cipher letter in sequence.

intentio.diplomatic: Ich bitte dich komm von stund an zu mir/ es thut sehr noth.
intentio.translation: I beg you, come to me at once; it is very urgent.
intentio.normalization: Lowercase the German, omit spaces and punctuation, and write u as v for comparison.

editorial_note: The 41 printed letters and the 45-letter normalized German agree in their first five decoded positions. At six, both the cipher line and the cover word bene give b. The key turns b into d. The German has t. The printed sources disagree here. Their wording does not establish how the difference arose.
provenance: Frankfurt, 1608, Herzog August Bibliothek Wolfenbüttel, Fb 243. Printed p. 56 describes the shift and diagrams the circle. Printed p. 57 gives the paired alphabet, German intention, significant letters and cover.
AI visual collation of HAB Fb 243 on 23 November 2026 checked all 41 types in the significant-letter line, the 22 printed pairs, the German and the 85-word prayer. No human review is documented.
The public evidence register preserves exact crops of the letter line and prayer. The earlier 42-letter transcription is retained in the correction history.
